reason: A cross-family consolidation result landed after 9.00. It found and fixed two real B6 source defects: inconsistent sub-family keying and non-deterministic use of Python hash() that changed emitted bytes across PYTHONHASHSEED values. The repaired B6 generator is byte-stable across varied hash seeds, its 12 tests still pass, and a sweep over all 14 candidate JSONL files found zero parse errors, zero canonical/training eligibility violations, and zero contradictory cross-family duplicate prompts. The same sweep exposed an unresolved tokenizer-ABI design mismatch: B0-B3 use 15 placeholder ordinals, B4 uses a disjoint 60-ordinal block, and B5 roughly 93 ordinals, for 168 distinct placeholder ordinals versus the course's declared 46 real accepted atoms. This is not yet proven fatal before real-tokenizer binding, but it is a concrete fail-closed admission blocker until the canonical ABI-binding layer demonstrates a deterministic, collision-safe, leakage-safe mapping or reduces the candidate symbol space. No training/admission/runtime/BASE/semantics credit is added.
